text.p: Manchester United manager Alex Ferguson defended his decision to field a weakened team despite losing 2-0 in the fourth round of the League Cup at Leicester on Wednesday.
Ferguson was without several key players because of injury but he still opted to leave out various experienced figures, including Eric Cantona, David Beckham and Nicky Butt.
It meant that centre-back David May and midfielder Roy Keane were the only regular first-team players included in the starting line-up.
But Ferguson said: "I still think the approach I have adopted was the right thing to do. You can't go for everything and this competition is providing good experience for our younger lads.
"I would have liked to have played a couple more experienced defenders tonight but it wasn't possible and I might also have included Peter Schmeichel but for a hand injury.
"However, even with the side I put out I know that those lads are capable of performing far better than that. What disappointed me was our passing. There were too many sloppy balls from us.

"But good luck to Leicester. They deserved to win. They are in the quarter-finals and it's good for a smaller club when they have a sniff of cup success. But I have to admit that next Wednesday's match with Rapid Vienna in the European Cup is a big game for us."
Leicester manager Martin O'Neill was delighted with his side's performance and was particularly full of praise for young Emile Heskey, who has made rapid strides since making his debut last season.
O'Neill said: "He was absolutely brilliant, fantastic at times tonight. He took his goal magnificently and his overall performance for an 18-year-old was tremendous.
"I have to keep pinching myself all the time to remember that he is so young considering the level of performance he has been turning in."
